payload.core_idea: A Learn-to-Rank (LTR) model serves as a meta-learner to optimally combine heterogeneous retrieval signals from multimodal transformers, unimodal text-to-text conversions, and image-to-image comparisons. This fusion architecture aggregates diverse evidence types to achieve competitive ranking performance that exceeds individual module capabilities.
payload.discussion: By training a dedicated ranking model, the work moves beyond simple averaging or heuristic selection, enabling a data-driven optimization of how different evidence sources contribute to the final decision. This is particularly valuable in complex disambiguation tasks where no single modality consistently dominates; for instance, text enrichment may resolve semantic ambiguity while image similarity confirms visual plausibility. The resulting system demonstrates that combining diverse architectural perspectives yields more robust and competitive results than isolated implementations.
payload.evidence: The text describes training a learn to rank (LTR) model in order to combine different modules, achieving competitive ranking results after exploring transformer-based methods, unimodal conversions, and LLM-based knowledge enhancement.
payload.idea_text: A Learn-to-Rank (LTR) model serves as a meta-learner to optimally combine heterogeneous retrieval signals from multimodal transformers, unimodal text-to-text conversions, and image-to-image comparisons. This fusion architecture aggregates diverse evidence types to achieve competitive ranking performance that exceeds individual module capabilities.
payload.mechanism: Individual modules process the input data according to their specific paradigms—some converting the problem to unimodal tasks while others perform direct cross-modal matching—and output relevance scores for candidate images. The Learn-to-Rank model takes these scores as features and trains on ground truth labels to predict the final ranking order. This mechanism effectively synthesizes the implicit knowledge captured by Chain-of-Thought prompting and the explicit visual-textual alignments from transformer models.

work_version_records.abstract: Visual Word Sense Disambiguation (VWSD) is a novel challenging task with the goal of retrieving an image among a set of candidates, which better represents the meaning of an ambiguous word within a given context. In this paper, we make a substantial step towards unveiling this interesting task by applying a varying set of approaches. Since VWSD is primarily a text-image retrieval task, we explore the latest transformer-based methods for multimodal retrieval. Additionally, we utilize Large Language Models (LLMs) as knowledge bases to enhance the given phrases and resolve ambiguity related to the target word. We also study VWSD as a unimodal problem by converting to text-to-text and image-to-image retrieval, as well as question-answering (QA), to fully explore the capabilities of relevant models. To tap into the implicit knowledge of LLMs, we experiment with Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting to guide explainable answer generation. On top of all, we train a learn to rank (LTR) model in order to combine our different modules, achieving competitive ranking results. Extensive experiments on VWSD demonstrate valuable insights to effectively drive future directions.
